definition: Spatial–temporal reasoning is an area of artificial intelligence that draws from the fields of computer science, cognitive science, and cognitive psychology.
details: The theoretic goal—on the cognitive side—involves representing and reasoning spatial-temporal knowledge in mind. The applied goal—on the computing side—involves developing high-level control systems of automata for navigating and understanding time and space.

explainer.lead: Spatial–temporal reasoning is an AI area drawing on computer science, cognitive science, and cognitive psychology. It matters on two fronts: modelling how minds represent space and time, and building control systems for automata that navigate and understand time and space.

tiers.eli5: It is about reasoning over both where things are and when things happen — like knowing a bus is at the corner now and will be two blocks away in a minute.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to high-level control of automata that must navigate and understand time and space. A pitfall is that the cognitive-side goal of representing spatial-temporal knowledge in mind and the computing-side control goal are distinct and do not automatically inform each other.
tiers.paperLevel: An area of AI drawing from computer science, cognitive science, and cognitive psychology; the theoretic goal is representing and reasoning about spatial-temporal knowledge in mind, and the applied goal is developing high-level control systems of automata for navigating and understanding time and space. No formula or specific limits are given.

explainer.example: A navigation system for an automaton uses spatial–temporal reasoning to track where it is and predict where it will be, feeding a high-level control system that decides its next move.
